items.title: 5.3 Equations of Medians, Altitudes and Right Bisectors (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 146-148: 5.3 Examples 7 (medians), 8 (altitudes), 9 (right bisectors) with Figures 5.2-5.4 and four Remember! boxes

blocks.text: Bachon, ab tak humne seekha ke line ki equation kaise banti hai. Ab is ilm ko triangle par lagate hain. Har triangle ke andar teen khaas qisam ki lines hoti hain: medians, altitudes aur right bisectors. Is section mein hum in sab ki equations nikalenge. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke koi naya formula nahi chahiye; sirf mid-point ka formula aur point-slope form, jo aap pehle se jaante hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har line ke liye ek point aur ek slope chahiye. Point hamesha maloom hota hai, sirf slope dhoondna parta hai:
Median: vertex (kona) aur saamne wali side ka mid-point. Do points maloom, to two-point form.
Altitude: vertex se guzarti hai aur saamne wali side par perpendicular (amood) hoti hai. Slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{side ka slope}}\).
Right bisector: side ke mid-point se guzarti hai aur usi side par perpendicular hoti hai.
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: altitude ka 'pair' vertex par, right bisector ka 'pair' mid-point par.

rows: vertex aur saamne wali side ka mid-point
blocks.caption: Hamara khulasa: median, altitude, right bisector

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Median triangle ke kisi vertex ko saamne wali side ke mid-point se milati hai.

Pehli misaal medians ki hai. Socho triangle gatte ka bana hua hai aur aap use ungli ki nok par balance karna chahte hain. Woh balance point teeno medians ke milne ki jagah (centroid) hai. Hum pehle teeno sides ke mid-points nikalenge, phir har vertex ko saamne wale mid-point se jorenge.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\) and \(C(-2, 7)\). Find the equations of medians of the triangle \(ABC\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\) aur \(C(-2, 7)\).
Maloom karna: teeno medians ki equations.
Tareeqa: pehle sides ke mid-points nikalein; phir har median ke do points maloom hon ge (vertex aur mid-point), to two-point form lagayenge.

Sides ke mid-points
Maan lijiye \(D\), \(E\) aur \(F\) tarteeb se sides \(BC\), \(AC\) aur \(AB\) ke mid-points hain.
\[D\left(\dfrac{4 + (-2)}{2}, \dfrac{5 + 7}{2}\right) = D(1, 6)\]
\[E\left(\dfrac{2 + (-2)}{2}, \dfrac{3 + 7}{2}\right) = E(0, 5)\]
\[F\left(\dfrac{2 + 4}{2}, \dfrac{3 + 5}{2}\right) = F(3, 4)\]
Kyun: \(A\) se median saamne wali side \(BC\) ke mid-point par jati hai, \(B\) se \(AC\) ke, aur \(C\) se \(AB\) ke. Mid-point = dono x ka average, dono y ka average.

Median AD
\[\dfrac{y - 3}{3 - 6} = \dfrac{x - 2}{2 - 1}\]
\[y - 3 = -3(x - 2)\]
\[3x + y - 9 = 0\]
Kyun: \(A(2, 3)\) aur \(D(1, 6)\) ke saath two-point form. \(\frac{y - 3}{-3} = x - 2\) se \(y - 3 = -3x + 6\), phir sab ek taraf.

Median BE
\[\dfrac{y - 5}{5 - 5} = \dfrac{x - 4}{4 - 0}\]
\[y - 5 = 0\]
Kyun: \(B(4, 5)\) aur \(E(0, 5)\) dono ka y-coordinate 5 hai, to slope \(\frac{5 - 5}{4 - 0} = 0\): leti hui (horizontal) line.
Dhyan dein: kitab ki fraction mein neeche 0 aa raha hai; yeh sirf likhne ka shortcut hai, asal matlab \(y - 5 = 0 \cdot (x - 4)\) hai. Zero se taqseem kabhi mat kijiye.

Median CF
\[\dfrac{y - 7}{7 - 4} = \dfrac{x + 2}{-2 - 3}\]
\[-5(y - 7) = 3(x + 2)\]
\[3x + 5y - 29 = 0\]
Kyun: \(C(-2, 7)\) aur \(F(3, 4)\) ke saath two-point form; cross-multiply se \(-5y + 35 = 3x + 6\), yani \(3x + 5y - 29 = 0\).

Tasdeeq:
\(D(1, 6)\): \(3 + 6 - 9 = 0\). \(F(3, 4)\): \(9 + 20 - 29 = 0\). Teeno medians centroid par milti hain:
\[G\left(\dfrac{2 + 4 - 2}{3}, \dfrac{3 + 5 + 7}{3}\right) = G\left(\dfrac{4}{3}, 5\right)\]
Aur waqai \(3 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 5 - 9 = 0\), \(y = 5\), \(3 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 25 - 29 = 0\). Teeno equations sahi hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow grid par cyan triangle A(2, 3), B(4, 5), C(-2, 7). Teen medians kaale rang mein: AD jo D(1, 6) tak, BE jo E(0, 5) tak aur CF jo F(3, 4) tak jati hai; teeno ek hi point par milte hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.2: Medians of triangle ABC (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.2)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Figure 5.2 mein dekhiye: kya teeno medians ek hi point se guzar rahi hain? Haan, \(G(\frac{4}{3}, 5)\) se. Yeh ittefaq nahi; har triangle mein aisa hota hai, aur Section 5.5 mein hum is ko saabit karenge.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Altitude woh line hai jo kisi vertex se saamne wali side par perpendicular kheenchi jaye.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Agar \(m_{1}\) aur \(m_{2}\) do perpendicular lines ke slopes hon to \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\) kyun? Line ko \(90^\circ\) ghumane se us ki direction \((1, m)\) badal kar \((-m, 1)\) ban jati hai, jis ka slope \(-\frac{1}{m}\) hai. Is liye perpendicular ka slope 'negative reciprocal' hota hai: fraction ulat do aur sign badal do. Misaal: slope \(\frac{3}{7}\) ho to perpendicular ka slope \(-\frac{7}{3}\). (Yeh tab chalta hai jab koi line vertical ya horizontal na ho.)

Doosri misaal altitudes ki hai. Altitude ko triangle ki 'unchai' samjhiye: jaise kisi deewar ki unchai naapne ke liye feeta bilkul seedha khara rakhte hain, waise hi altitude vertex se saamne wali side par seedha (\(90^\circ\) par) girta hai. Har altitude ke liye teen qadam: side ka slope, us ka negative reciprocal, aur vertex se point-slope form.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(5, -1)\) and \(C(-2, -4)\) are the vertices of \(\triangle ABC\). Find the equations of altitudes of triangle \(ABC\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(5, -1)\), \(C(-2, -4)\).
Maloom karna: teeno altitudes ki equations.
Tareeqa: altitude vertex se guzarti hai aur saamne wali side par perpendicular hoti hai. Har ek ke liye: side ka slope, phir perpendicular slope \(-\frac{1}{m}\), phir vertex se point-slope form.
Maan lijiye \(\overline{AE}\), \(\overline{BF}\) aur \(\overline{CD}\) tarteeb se sides \(BC\), \(CA\) aur \(AB\) par altitudes hain.

Altitude AE: slopes
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{-4 - (-1)}{-2 - 5} = \dfrac{3}{7}\]
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{AE} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{BC}} = -\dfrac{7}{3}\]
Kyun: \(AE \perp BC\), is liye dono slopes ka product \(-1\) hai. \(\frac{-3}{-7} = \frac{3}{7}\); minus taqseem minus plus.

Altitude AE: equation
\[y - 2 = -\dfrac{7}{3}(x - 1)\]
\[3y - 6 = -7x + 7\]
\[7x + 3y - 13 = 0\]
Kyun: vertex \(A(1, 2)\) se point-slope form; fraction khatam karne ke liye 3 se multiply kiya.

Altitude BF: slopes
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{CA} = \dfrac{2 - (-4)}{1 - (-2)} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2\]
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BF} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{CA}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(BF \perp CA\). 2 ka negative reciprocal \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

Altitude BF: equation
\[y + 1 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 5)\]
\[x + 2y - 3 = 0\]
Kyun: \(B(5, -1)\) se point-slope; \(y - (-1) = y + 1\). 2 se multiply: \(2y + 2 = -x + 5\).

Altitude CD: slopes
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{-1 - 2}{5 - 1} = -\dfrac{3}{4}\]
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{CD} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{AB}} = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: \(CD \perp AB\); \(-\frac{3}{4}\) ka negative reciprocal \(+\frac{4}{3}\) hai (do minus mil kar plus).

Altitude CD: equation
\[y + 4 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x + 2)\]
\[4x - 3y - 4 = 0\]
Kyun: \(C(-2, -4)\) se point-slope; 3 se multiply: \(3y + 12 = 4x + 8\).

Tasdeeq:
Har vertex apni altitude par hai: \(A\): \(7 + 6 - 13 = 0\); \(B\): \(5 - 2 - 3 = 0\); \(C\): \(-8 + 12 - 4 = 0\). \(AE\) aur \(BF\) ko hal karne se \((\frac{17}{11}, \frac{8}{11})\) milta hai, aur \(4 \cdot \frac{17}{11} - 3 \cdot \frac{8}{11} - 4 = \frac{68 - 24 - 44}{11} = 0\). Yani teeno altitudes ek point (orthocentre) par milti hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow grid par cyan triangle A(1, 2), B(5, -1), C(-2, -4), konon par dots. Teen altitudes (oonchaiyan) kaale rang mein: AE, BF aur CD; un ke paon D, E, F par right angle (90 darje) ke nishan hain, aur teeno ek point par milti hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.3: Altitudes of triangle ABC (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.3)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 8 mein altitude \(AE\) ki equation \(7x + 3y - 13 = 0\) hai aur side \(BC\) ka slope \(\frac{3}{7}\). \(AE\) ka slope \(-\frac{7}{3}\) hai. Product: \(\frac{3}{7} \times \left(-\frac{7}{3}\right) = -1\). Har altitude ke liye yeh chhota test zaroor kijiye.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Triangle ka perpendicular ya right bisector woh line hai jo triangle ki kisi side par perpendicular ho aur us side ke mid point se guzre.

Teesri misaal right bisectors ki hai. Right bisector ko aise samjhiye: do gharon ke darmiyan aisi deewar banani hai jis ka har point dono gharon se baraabar faasle par ho. Woh deewar dono gharon ko milane wali line ke mid-point se guzregi aur us par perpendicular hogi. Yahi right bisector hai.

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(-3, 2)\), \(B(5, 4)\) and \(C(3, -8)\). Find the equations of right bisectors of triangle \(ABC\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(-3, 2)\), \(B(5, 4)\), \(C(3, -8)\).
Maloom karna: teeno right bisectors ki equations.
Tareeqa: right bisector side ke mid-point se guzarta hai aur usi side par perpendicular hota hai. Har side ke liye: mid-point, side ka slope, negative reciprocal, point-slope form.

Sides ke mid-points
Maan lijiye \(D\), \(E\) aur \(F\) tarteeb se sides \(BC\), \(CA\) aur \(AB\) ke mid-points hain.
\[D\left(\dfrac{5 + 3}{2}, \dfrac{4 + (-8)}{2}\right) = D(4, -2)\]
\[E\left(\dfrac{-3 + 3}{2}, \dfrac{2 + (-8)}{2}\right) = E(0, -3)\]
\[F\left(\dfrac{-3 + 5}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 4}{2}\right) = F(1, 3)\]
Kyun: har right bisector inhi mein se kisi ek point se guzrega.

AB ka right bisector
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{4 - 2}{5 - (-3)} = \dfrac{2}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}\]
\[\text{Slope of right bisector to } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{AB}} = -4\]
\[y - 3 = -4(x - 1)\]
\[4x + y - 7 = 0\]
Kyun: mid-point \(F(1, 3)\) se, perpendicular slope ke saath point-slope form. \(y - 3 = -4x + 4\).

BC ka right bisector
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{-8 - 4}{3 - 5} = \dfrac{-12}{-2} = 6\]
\[\text{Slope of right bisector to } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{BC}} = -\dfrac{1}{6}\]
\[y + 2 = -\dfrac{1}{6}(x - 4)\]
\[x + 6y + 8 = 0\]
Kyun: \(D(4, -2)\) se; 6 se multiply: \(6y + 12 = -x + 4\).

CA ka right bisector
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{CA} = \dfrac{2 - (-8)}{-3 - 3} = \dfrac{10}{-6} = -\dfrac{5}{3}\]
\[\text{Slope of right bisector to } \overline{CA} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{CA}} = \dfrac{3}{5}\]
\[y + 3 = \dfrac{3}{5}(x - 0)\]
\[3x - 5y - 15 = 0\]
Kyun: \(E(0, -3)\) se; 5 se multiply: \(5y + 15 = 3x\).
Dhyan dein: \(2 - (-8) = 10\) hai, 6 nahi.

Tasdeeq:
Pehle do bisectors ko hal karne se \(O(\frac{50}{23}, -\frac{39}{23})\) milta hai; phir \(3 \cdot \frac{50}{23} - 5\left(-\frac{39}{23}\right) - 15 = \frac{150 + 195 - 345}{23} = 0\), yani teeno \(O\) par milte hain. Saath hi \(OA^{2} = OB^{2} = OC^{2} = \frac{21386}{529}\): \(O\) teeno vertices se baraabar faasle par hai (circumcentre), kyunke right bisector ka har point side ke dono siron se baraabar door hota hai.
blocks.answer: Right bisector of \(\overline{AB}\): \(4x + y - 7 = 0\); of \(\overline{BC}\): \(x + 6y + 8 = 0\); of \(\overline{CA}\): \(3x - 5y - 15 = 0\).

blocks.alt: Pale yellow grid par cyan triangle A(-3, 2), B(5, 4), C(3, -8). Sides ke right bisectors kaale rang mein mid-points F(1, 3), D(4, -2) aur E(0, -3) se guzarte hain, har ek apni side par perpendicular (right angle ke nishan ke saath), aur teeno ek point par milte hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.4: Right bisectors of the sides of triangle ABC (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.4)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Right bisector \(4x + y - 7 = 0\) par koi bhi point lijiye, jaise \(x = 2\) rakhne se \((2, -1)\). Is ka \(A(-3, 2)\) se faasla: \(\sqrt{25 + 9} = \sqrt{34}\). \(B(5, 4)\) se faasla: \(\sqrt{9 + 25} = \sqrt{34}\). Baraabar! Right bisector ka har point side ke dono siron se baraabar door hota hai; isi liye teeno right bisectors ka common point teeno vertices se baraabar door hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Tasdeeq ke liye do lines ka intersection point kaise nikalein? Misaal: \(7x + 3y - 13 = 0\) aur \(x + 2y - 3 = 0\).
Doosri equation se \(x = 3 - 2y\). Is ko pehli mein rakhiye:
\[7(3 - 2y) + 3y - 13 = 0\]
\[8 - 11y = 0\]
Yani \(y = \frac{8}{11}\) aur \(x = 3 - \frac{16}{11} = \frac{17}{11}\). Phir yeh point teesri equation mein rakh kar dekhiye: agar zero aaye to teeno lines concurrent (ek point par milne wali) hain aur aap ki equations sahi hain. Yeh substitution ka wohi tareeqa hai jo aap ne Class IX-X mein simultaneous equations ke liye seekha tha.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ek hi triangle mein median aur altitude ka farq dekhiye. Example 7 wale triangle \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\), \(C(-2, 7)\) mein \(A\) se altitude:
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{7 - 5}{-2 - 4} = -\dfrac{1}{3}\]
Altitude ka slope 3, aur \(A(2, 3)\) se: \(y - 3 = 3(x - 2)\), yani \(3x - y - 3 = 0\).
Median \(AD\) thi \(3x + y - 9 = 0\). Dono \(A\) se guzarti hain magar mukhtalif lines hain: median mid-point par jati hai, altitude perpendicular girti hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: In sawalon mein marks har line ke alag milte hain. Har line ke shuru mein saaf likhiye: 'Slope of BC = ...', 'Slope of altitude = ...', 'Equation of altitude AE is ...'. Aakhir mein teeno lines ka common point nikal kar check kar lein; agar teeno ek point par na milein to kahin ghalti hai. Yeh check do minute leta hai aur poora sawal bacha leta hai.

Ek nazar peeche: teeno misaalon mein kaam ka dhaancha ek hi tha. Pehle socha ke line kis point se guzarti hai (vertex ya mid-point). Phir socha ke slope kahan se aayega (do points se, ya perpendicular hone ki wajah se negative reciprocal). Aakhir mein point-slope form laga kar general form tak simplify kiya aur common point se tasdeeq ki. Exercise 5.1 ke sawalon mein bhi bilkul yahi dhaancha chalega, sirf numbers badlenge. Aur Section 5.5 mein hum yeh bhi saabit karenge ke yeh teeno qisam ki lines har triangle mein hamesha ek ek point par milti hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Median: vertex + saamne wali side ka mid-point; two-point form.
2. Altitude: vertex se, slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{saamne wali side ka slope}}\).
3. Right bisector: side ke mid-point se, slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{usi side ka slope}}\).
4. Perpendicular lines: \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\).
5. Tasdeeq: kisi triangle ki teeno medians (altitudes, right bisectors) hamesha ek point par milti hain; is point se teeno equations check kijiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Altitude ko mid-point se, ya right bisector ko vertex se guzar dena. Altitude: vertex. Right bisector: mid-point.
2. Negative reciprocal mein sign na badalna: slope 6 ka perpendicular \(-\frac{1}{6}\) hai, \(\frac{1}{6}\) nahi.
3. Vertex ko ghalat mid-point se jor dena: \(A\) se median \(BC\) ke mid-point par jati hai, \(AB\) ke nahi.
4. Slope formula mein negative coordinates ke saath sign ki ghalti, jaise \(2 - (-8) = 10\).
